source.report: Archinal et al., Report of the IAU Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements: 2015, CMDA 130:22 (2018), Table 1
source.lunar_model: WGCCRE 2009, as retained by pck00011: the 2015 report no longer tabulates lunar rotational elements. IAU_MOON approximates the Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame, not the binary-PCK MOON_PA/MOON_ME models.

time_scale: UTC input converted independently through TAI, TT, then geocentric TDB (Fairhead-Bretagnon, no topocentric term)
units: Dimensionless direction cosines; matrices are flattened row-major
frame: ICRF to the named IAU body-fixed axes. NAIF PCK uses the historical J2000 label for ICRF. Both module coordinate systems use an Earth origin; axis-body identity is independent of origin.

generator.recipe:
import erfa, spiceypy as spice
spice.kclear()
spice.furnsh('pck00011.tpc')  # validate the SHA256 above first
utc = erfa.dtf2d('UTC', 2007, 4, 5, 12, 0, 0.0)
tai = erfa.utctai(*utc)
tt = erfa.taitt(*tai)
dtr = erfa.dtdb(*tt, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
tdb = erfa.tttdb(*tt, dtr)
days = (tdb[0] - 2451545.0) + tdb[1]
# for each listed case:
matrix = spice.pxform('J2000', case['frame'], days * 86400.0).reshape(-1).tolist()
spice.kclear()
generator.independence: The matrices are generated by published NAIF CSPICE/PCK; time conversion uses separately installed PyERFA. Neither generator calls the new module or its C++ body model.

tolerance_rationale: 1e-12 for the Moon and 1e-11 for the other bodies allow binary64 epoch conversion, prime-meridian multiplication/reduction and Euler evaluation. The fast planetary rotations have prime meridians up to 2.4 million degrees at this epoch, magnifying floating-point operation-order differences. The tolerance is much smaller than omitting TT-to-TDB or any significant periodic term; it measures reproduction of the analytical PCK model, not physical orientation accuracy.
